score.doctor_final_text: This means the herniated disc at the L5-S1 level is pinching your nerve, which is causing the sharp pain radiating down your leg. For next steps, we will focus on conservative management, including physical therapy, activity modification, and pain management. DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 disc herniation with lumbar radiculopathy

dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent, and I'll be evaluating your back and leg pain today. To help me understand what's going on, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your leg, or any recent changes in your bowel or bladder control?
No, I haven't had any numbness or tingling, and my bowel and bladder function have been completely normal. The pain is really sharp though, especially when I try to move or bend.
Got it, thank you for sharing that. Did this pain start suddenly after a specific action, like lifting something heavy or twisting, and how far down your leg does it go?

Yes, it started suddenly while I was doing exercises at the gym - I think I was doing some deadlifts when I felt this sharp pain shoot through my lower back. The pain goes all the way down the side of my leg and into my foot.

That sounds like a very painful experience, especially coming on so suddenly during deadlifts. Does the pain worsen when you cough, sneeze, or sit down, and do you feel any weakness when you try to lift your foot or big toe?

I haven't really noticed if coughing or sneezing makes it worse since I've been trying to stay still, but sitting definitely makes the pain more intense. I don't think I have any weakness - I can still move my foot and toes, it just hurts a lot when I do.
Thank you for providing those details, as they help narrow things down. To help me get a clearer picture of your symptoms, does the pain improve at all when you lie down flat on your back?

Yes, actually lying flat does seem to help a bit - the pain isn't quite as sharp when I'm completely flat on my back. But as soon as I try to get up or change position, that shooting pain comes right back.

That is very helpful to know, as relief with lying flat is quite common with certain disc issues. To help me visualize exactly what is happening in your spine, I would like to order an imaging study.

This means the herniated disc at the L5-S1 level is pinching your nerve, which is causing the sharp pain radiating down your leg.
